record.paper_title: Constructive Field Theory and Applications: Perspectives and Open Problems
record.original_question: Develop a rigorous non-perturbative mean-field theory for condensed-matter models such as the Hubbard model, namely a non-perturbative version of the dynamical mean-field or d = ∞ limit.

evidence.quote: Develop a rigorous non-perturbative mean-field theory for condensed matter, i.e. develop the non-perturbative version of the dynamical mean-field or d = ∞ limit of models such as the Hubbard model

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Hubbard model on the d-dimensional hypercubic lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$, defined by the Hamiltonian
$$ H = -t \sum_{\langle x,y\rangle,\,\sigma\in\{\uparrow,\downarrow\}} \big(c^\dagger_{x,\sigma} c_{y,\sigma} + c^\dagger_{y,\sigma} c_{x,\sigma}\big) + U \sum_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d} n_{x,\uparrow} n_{x,\downarrow} - \mu \sum_{x,\sigma} n_{x,\sigma}, $$
where $c^\dagger_{x,\sigma}, c_{x,\sigma}$ are fermionic creation/annihilation operators on site $x$ with spin $\sigma$, $n_{x,\sigma} = c^\dagger_{x,\sigma}c_{x,\sigma}$, $\langle x,y\rangle$ denotes nearest-neighbour pairs, $t>0$ is the hopping amplitude, $U\in\mathbb{R}$ is the on-site interaction, and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$ is the chemical potential. In the formal limit $d\to\infty$ with the hopping rescaled as $t\to t/\sqrt{2d}$, physicists have introduced a "dynamical mean-field theory" (DMFT) in which the lattice problem reduces to a self-consistent single-site quantum impurity problem coupled to a self-consistently determined bath, with a momentum-independent self-energy.

The problem is to construct this DMFT (equivalently, the $d=\infty$ limit of the Hubbard model and analogous interacting lattice fermion models) rigorously and non-perturbatively. Specifically:

(a) Define, on a mathematically rigorous level, the infinite-volume Gibbs (KMS) states (or zero-temperature ground states) of the Hubbard model in the suitably rescaled $d\to\infty$ limit, without recourse to formal perturbation expansions.

(b) Prove that the resulting limiting theory is described by a self-consistent single-site effective action / impurity model, with a self-energy $\Sigma(\omega)$ that is independent of lattice momentum, and establish convergence (in an appropriate sense, e.g. convergence of finite-volume Green's functions or local observables) of the finite-$d$ model to this limit.

(c) Establish non-perturbative properties of this limiting theory, such as existence and analyticity (or non-analyticity) of thermodynamic functions, existence of phase transitions (e.g. Mott metal–insulator transition), and uniqueness or multiplicity of solutions to the DMFT self-consistency equations.

Provide such a rigorous non-perturbative construction, or alternatively rule it out.
artifact.status_search_result: A rigorous non-perturbative construction of the dynamical mean-field theory ($d=\infty$ limit) of the Hubbard model is widely cited as an outstanding open problem in mathematical physics and constructive field theory. While DMFT is extensively used in physics (Metzner–Vollhardt, Georges–Kotliar et al.) and partial rigorous results exist for related impurity / mean-field fermionic models, no complete rigorous non-perturbative construction of the Hubbard $d=\infty$ limit appears in the literature as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Dynamical mean-field theory of strongly correlated fermion systems
status_evidence.snippet: Review by Georges, Kotliar, Krauth, Rozenberg describing DMFT and the $d\to\infty$ limit at a physics level of rigor, with self-consistency equations for a momentum-independent self-energy.
status_evidence.claim: DMFT is defined and used non-rigorously in physics; a rigorous construction is not provided.

status_evidence.title: Correlated lattice fermions in high dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Metzner and Vollhardt introduce the $d\to\infty$ limit of the Hubbard model with hopping rescaled as $t/\sqrt{2d}$.
status_evidence.claim: The $d=\infty$ limit is defined formally; no rigorous non-perturbative construction.
